analysis.title: JPM Tyler - Morning Briefing: Fut higher led by Tech; Bullish Credit Signal; MU / PCE post mortem; ISM Preview; Trading Desk Conf Call 1 Oct 2026
key_insights: Futures are higher led by Tech: SPX +0.2%, NDX +0.6%, RTY -0.2%. Mag7, Memory, Semis and Software are all higher pre-market. RTY struggles with higher yields, and more than 40% of the index is unprofitable companies, though squeeze risk exists with a Middle East deal.

Longer-dated yields continue to make multi-decade highs, with the 10Y at 5.317%. JPM frames this as a growth story as the bond market reprices around a higher R*, which equities should digest. The 10Y averaged 6.65% in the 1990s and stocks were fine. Bonds are oversold but may take time to find support.
USD set a new 52-week high this morning. With yields and the dollar higher, the market seems comfortable reverting to portions of the Q2 playbook dominated by Tech and Semis.
Today's focus is ISM-Mfg, with NFP tomorrow possibly surprising to the upside given the ADP print. JPM says if unemployment stays at 4.0% or higher, bonds will not move to price additional hikes.

EU and UK markets are lower, with the region acting as a funding short for US and Asia Tech plays. UKX -1.5%, SX5E -0.9%, DAX -0.8%. APAC was stronger, with NKY +3.3% and KOSPI +1.9% on the AI trade, and ASX -2.0% the laggard.

The PCE print, income, spending and Q2 revisions point to a strong economy that is getting stronger. The PCE print plus Fed's Williams' comments cut October hike expectations from 70% on Monday to 37% yesterday.

The 10Y yield reversed higher by about 11bp yesterday and closed +6bp. The bear steepening shifted flows from an RTY-led squeeze to a concentrated Tech trade. Mag7 and Software led, Semis were up small, and Memory lagged by more than 2%.
ISM Prices Paid sub-indices tend to precede CPI by 2-3 months, and ISM-Srvcs Prices Paid is the more impactful. JPM says Prices Paid in today's ISM-Mfg may matter more than the headline.

Alexa Hanelin (bonds) says the bear steepening is less about inflation and more about the growth story. Term premium remains under pressure from the fiscal backdrop. Buying today has been concentrated in the belly, from banks, extension asset managers and foreign real money.

Saul Doctor's credit Fear & Greed Index is at 83, above the 80 trigger level, a bullish credit signal. CDS spreads widened as TLT 3-month ATM implied vol rose from 10% to 15%. CDX.IG is just shy of 60bp, 6bp off the YTD wides, and the 3-month time-value of CDX.IG is 30c.
Feroli expects ISM-Mfg at 54.5 vs 54.6 prior, with continued strength in new orders and output. He is concerned about inflationary pressure from higher energy prices.

MU post-mortem (Josh Meyers): a strong print and solid guide, and management anticipates F1Q to be the floor for gross margins in fiscal 2027. The stock was up over 4% early, then flipped negative with no obvious reason.

MU concerns raised: F2H27 capex greater than F1H with no size given, server commentary seen as sugar-coating de-specing, a lack of clarity on when capital return reaches 100% payout, and a rise in Days of Inventory. Meyers suspects shares trade higher in a neutral market.

Sanjay's answer on LTAs left the door open to less than 50% LTA coverage, which would change the existing investment thesis. MU expects the supply-demand environment to tighten further in 2027 and 2028.

August core PCE deflator rose 0.25% m/m, in line with JPM's forecast. The y/y rate was 3.01% vs JPM's 3.28% forecast, and the 3-month pace is 2.05%. The y/y rate is still at or just above 3.0% in each of the last six months, so there is little progress toward 2%.

The July core PCE y/y rate was revised down 36bp, largely from methodology revisions to software, portfolio management fees and legal services. Real spending rose 0.6% m/m. The saving rate was revised up, with July going from 3.0% to 4.6% and August at 4.1%.

Market Intel calls the PCE print great for bulls, with inflation below expectations and the prior month revised lower. It expects a squeezy session with broad participation, and if the week's data continues the trend, EU to outperform the US and RTY to lead SPX and NDX.

Nikos: leverage and positioning excesses that unwound in June/July have partly rebuilt. Equity futures leverage is near YTD highs, CTAs are rebuilding tech-index longs, and margin-account leverage is still very elevated. Fundamentals cushion the downside, with hyperscaler capex revised to 2026E $805bn and 2027E $1.1tr. A renewed shock looks like a dip-to-buy in tech/AI.
Nikos on bonds: rebalancing inflows explain about half the flow gap, but duration-adjusted flow is about half the nominal pace, so inflows are not anchoring yields.

Nikos on FX: spec and CTA positioning is short EUR and long USD (DXY > 100, EUR < 1.14). Corporate hedgers who had drifted long EUR / short USD are scrambling back toward neutral, pressuring EUR down and USD up, with room to run.

JPM Market Intel returns to Tactically Bullish, after moving to Cautious/Neutral on Aug 31. Since then SPX is +75bp and the +NDX / -RTY pair returned 7.9%. JPM sees bond yields finding a level and oil likely to trend lower, albeit choppily.

Rationale for the bullish view: strong flash PMIs, consumer strength, 26Q3 earnings expectations of about 29% that may prove light, bond yields that may stabilize, and improving technicals. Jay Barry sees the 10Y moving from 5.18% to 5.20% over the next month and ending the year at 5.05%.

Longer-term concerns: the bond market may underprice the Fed hiking cycle given 5% real growth per flash PMIs, a possible 50bp move at a Fed meeting, Ag inflation bleeding into core, and whether anything but Tech can work.

Monetization menu: stay long Tech, but no longer pair it with an RTY short because of squeeze risk from lower oil/yields, and use a derivative expression to play the squeeze. Within Tech, Semis and Mag7 may outperform. Software is a non-consensus bullish play. Ex-AI, JPM favors Banks.

A US/Iran deal is the biggest catalyst and would squeeze EU and RTY higher. The COVID Reopening theme (Airlines, Autos, Cruise Lines, Hotels) is also of interest, preferably via options. Rate sensitives like Real Estate, Telecom and Utilities may participate in a squeeze but likely lag the SPX ex-AI.

FactSet 26Q3 expectations: 11.9% revenue growth, 28.9% earnings growth, 15.0% margins. 26Q4: 11.7% revenue growth and 2.5% earnings growth. FY26: 12.1% revenue and 31.8% EPS growth. FY27: 9.1% revenue and 15.2% EPS growth. 26Q2 printed 15.6% revenue growth, 52.3% earnings growth and 17% margins.

S&P 500 26Q3 FactSet consensus estimate: 11.9% revenue growth, 28.9% earnings growth, 15.0% margins. 26Q2 reported 15.6% revenue growth, 52.3% earnings growth and 17.0% margins.

26Q3 would be the third consecutive quarter of 10%+ revenue growth and 25%+ earnings growth. Margin expectations are the second best quarter ever, below 26Q2's 17.0% and above 26Q1's record 14.8%.
